title: wsaw scan result
description: One scan of one target in one consent mode. This schema is wsaw's primary interface: reports, the web interface and CSV exports are all derived views over it. Changes are additive by default; removing or repurposing a field is a breaking change.

target.description: Configured target name; stable across scans, which is what ties history together.

consentMode.description: Part of a result's identity. Results are never compared across modes.

termination.description: Why capture stopped. Anything other than idle means the asset list may be incomplete and must not be read as 'nothing was loaded'.

error.description: Set when the scan failed. Its presence invalidates the asset list.

attempt.description: Which attempt of a retried scan produced this result, counting from 1. Absent when retrying is disabled.

attempts.description: How many attempts were allowed for this scan.

previousError.description: Why the attempt before this one failed. Absent on a first attempt.

superseded.description: True on a failed result that a later attempt replaced. The failure remains in the history, but a superseded result is not what the next scan is compared against.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems a reader must see, such as a body that could not be fingerprinted.

outcome.description: 'not-needed' means no interaction was required, which is a legitimate and common result, not an error. 'unverified' means the interaction ran but its effect could not be confirmed.

mechanism.description: How the state was reached. A TCF API call is strong evidence; a heuristic label match is weak.

heuristic.description: True when the banner was found by guessing at button labels. Such results should be treated with caution.

userAgent.description: Empty means the browser's own user agent was used.

extraHeaderNames.description: Header names only. Values may be credentials and are never serialized.

warmCache.description: True means counts are not comparable with cold-cache scans.

browserRuntime.description: "local" when the browser ran as a host process, or the container runtime that ran it. A result is comparable with another only if a reader can see which rendered it.

browserImage.description: Container image, pinned by digest, when the browser ran in a container.

browserSandbox.description: Whether Chrome's own sandbox was active. In a container the container is the boundary and the inner sandbox is normally off, which is a material fact about the scan.

browserReused.description: True when the browser process had already served another scan, so isolation rested on clearing state rather than on the process boundary.

normalizedUrl.description: The diffing key. Stored so a reader can see exactly what was compared.

phase.description: Whether the request was observed before or after the consent action. A request already in flight keeps the phase it started in.

nonNetwork.description: data:, blob: and similar. Recorded, but nothing left the browser.

bodyUnavailable.description: Why no digest was taken. A missing digest is always explained rather than silently absent.

bodyRef.description: Reference to the stored response body, present when body storage is on. Bodies live outside this document as content-addressed files; fetch one with GET /api/v1/artifacts/{ref}.

body.description: The stored response body itself. Present only in an export — a HAR, a downloaded result, or the API's result endpoint — and never in the document as stored, which keeps bodies outside it. A result read from the store therefore has bodyRef and no body.

bodyEncoding.description: Present when body is base64-encoded because the bytes are not text. Absent when body is the body as text.

bodyStoredSize.description: How many bytes of the body were kept. Smaller than decodedSize when the size cap truncated it, which is the difference between a short body and a truncated one.

valueSha256.description: Cookie values are fingerprinted, never stored: they routinely contain identifiers.
